policy: Frozen twelve cases previously marked unresolved in PR #141; cannot be modified by later outcome rewriting or abandoned as already resolved

cases.prior_conclusion: Baal-zebub of Ekron in 2 Kings 1 and Beelzebul/Satan of the Gospels may be related names, not proven identical ancient entities; canonical conflation awaits independent textual judgment.
Leviticus 14:4 and Numbers 19:6 say cedar wood; the specific Phoenician juniper botanical taxon is an interpretation not certifiable from the Hebrew word alone.
Isaiah 44:14's ancient tree terms have competing botanical identifications; Aleppo pine cannot be established as a direct Hebrew species attribution.
The inherited Ai/Ayyah/Aiath equivalence in 1 Chronicles 7:28 and Nehemiah 11:31 is historically uncertain; the canonical links are not yet independently certified.
The source's strong Aiath-to-Ai canonical and alternate-label assertion is not established by 1 Chronicles 7:28; more than lexical resemblance is needed.
Acts 23:31 names Antipatris, not Aphek; an exact ancient site-identification requires independently supported archaeological evidence.
Isaiah 15:5 and Jeremiah 48:34 may use a proper Moabite site or a three-year-old heifer simile; philological identification remains disputed.
The equivalence of 2 Kings 11:6 Gate Sur and 2 Chronicles 23:5 Foundation Gate has not been independently proved.
Judges 9:37 Tabbur-erez is not directly named Gerizim; previous false aliases were removed but the remaining site assumption needs evidence.
Ezekiel 38:6 explicitly names a people Gomer, not a standalone written region; the record's place-versus-people semantics need review.
Jeremiah 48:1 Hebrew means stronghold but can be construed as the place Misgab; the proper-noun reading remains uncertain.
1 Samuel 22:6 has Saul on a height at Gibeah, not a clearly separate proper-named Ramah settlement; exact identity unproved.
